name: Real tennis
summary: Real tennis is the original indoor racket game from which lawn tennis took its name, played across a net in a walled hall whose sloping roofs, galleries and buttress are all part of play. Each court is unique, and its distinctive chase rule means some rallies are decided later rather than on the spot.

children.text: Real tennis is played indoors in a long walled hall divided by a net. Three of the walls carry a sloping roof, the penthouse, and the ball may be played off it, off the walls and into openings around the court.

Its best-known quirk is the chase. Some rallies end not with a point but with a mark of where the ball fell, and the players later swap ends and replay to see whether that mark can be beaten. Scoring otherwise looks familiar to a lawn tennis player, with games and sets.

relatedSports.note: Lawn tennis grew out of real tennis and kept much of its scoring.

name: Real tennis court
summary: A real tennis court is an indoor hall with a net across the middle, sloping roofs along three walls and openings that score when the ball goes in. No two courts are exactly alike, so there is no single standard size.
nonStandardNote: Every real tennis court is different. They share a layout, with a sloping penthouse roof along three walls, galleries beneath it, the dedans behind the service end, the grille and the angled tambour at the hazard end, and chase lines marked across the floor, but the floor size, the placing of the openings and the tambour vary from court to court, because most courts were built individually over several centuries.
